title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: No new session over the weekend — stocks head into the week still in correction territory after Friday's AI-led rout (S&P 500 -3.7% to 6,910; Nasdaq -5.3% to 22,618), the worst week since April 2025 (S&P -8.6% for the week).
Markets: The VIX closed near 37 Friday, up sharply from ~20 at the start of last week; a Thanksgiving-shortened session begins Monday (half day Friday).

Companies: Nvidia remains the focal point heading into the week amid a reported SEC inquiry into its disclosures, following Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation as CEO; CFO Colette Kress continues as interim chief.
Companies: Anthropic's newly listed shares are hovering just above their $83 IPO price after giving back their first-day pop in the broader tech selloff.
Companies: Recent M&A still digesting: Marvell's ~$115B all-stock deal for Lumentum, Fox's ~$22B Roku acquisition, and CVS Health's plan to split into two public companies.
Macro/Policy: Prediction markets now lean toward a 25bp Fed rate HIKE (not a cut) at the Dec. 9 meeting, a reversal from earlier cut bets after hotter-than-expected inflation data.
Macro/Policy: Week ahead: holiday-shortened trading, the October PCE inflation report, consumer confidence data, and earnings from Dell, Best Buy, Dollar Tree and Deere.
